pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Our Vision
Our vision is for Skinners’ Academy to be a highly successful, aspirational, inclusive and vibrant learning community in which all students are able to thrive academically and socially, achieve excellent outcomes that support their future ambitions, feel safe and supported because of strong and respectful relationships with staff and peers, and are enabled to become active and thoughtful citizens who are well-equipped to navigate the challenges and benefit from the opportunities of wider society and the adult world.
Our Culture
To make this vision a reality, we are guided by our Academy motto of ‘Be The Best You Can Be’.
Our culture is one of ‘high challenge, high support’ because it is this that allows all members of the Academy’s community to be their very best and fulfil their potential.
Our Values
At Skinners’ Academy, our values shape the character of our community and support every student in becoming the best version of themselves. They guide our actions, interactions, and ambitions, both within and beyond the classroom.
Kindness is at the heart of a respectful and inclusive school community. We promote empathy, compassion, and understanding, recognising that every action, no matter how small, has the power to uplift others and strengthen relationships.
We nurture a spirit of curiosity by encouraging students to ask questions, explore new ideas, and develop a lifelong love of learning. Curiosity drives innovation and critical thinking, helping learners connect with the world around them in meaningful and engaging ways.
We support students in developing the courage to take risks, speak up, and face challenges with resilience. Being brave means embracing failure as part of learning, standing up for what’s right, and believing in one’s ability to grow and make a difference.

pageCache.text:
Ancient Company, Modern Mission
Skinners’ Academy is proud to be part of a centuries-old legacy through its close partnership with The Skinners’ Company - a historic institution with a thoroughly modern purpose. Founded over 700 years ago, The Skinners’ Company has evolved from its traditional roots into a forward-thinking organisation dedicated to education, opportunity, and community impact.
Today, this commitment is brought to life through the Skinners’ Charity Foundation (SCF), which continues to invest in young people and their futures. In 2024/25 alone, the Foundation reached new heights - awarding more grants than ever before and supporting initiatives across vocational development, poverty relief, arts and heritage, and bursaries at three London universities. The scale of this support is reflected in 324 volunteering hours given, £147,505 donated, and the generosity of 85 member donors.
At Skinners’ Academy, this partnership has a direct and meaningful impact. Through the Skinners’ Educational Foundation (SEF), Equal Access grants are provided each year to ensure that every student can fully participate in school life, regardless of background. With 63% of our students eligible for free school meals - significantly above the national average - this support is vital.
These grants help fund essential school uniforms for those experiencing financial hardship. They also subsidise enriching experiences such as Activities Week, where students can take part in trips and hands-on learning opportunities - from visits to Southend’s Adventure Island, Go-Karting, Kayaking, Tocca Social and much more - without financial barriers. This year, the Equal Access grant has also contributed to funding new indoor multi-gym equipment, creating a lasting resource that will benefit current students and future generations alike.
This powerful partnership reflects a shared belief: that every young person deserves access to opportunity, enrichment, and success. The Skinners’ Company’s enduring heritage is matched by its commitment to shaping brighter futures today - making it an invaluable part of the Skinners’ Academy community.

Acting Principal Ms. R Adediran
Senior Executive Leader Ian Anderson

pageCache.text:
Principal's Welcome
Welcome to Skinners’ Academy, a co-educational academy in the north of Hackney. The Academy began life as the Skinners’ Company’s School for Girls in Stamford Hill in 1890.
The girls’ school closed in 2010, relocating to a new site in Woodberry Grove and reopening as a co-educational school, with the sixth form opening shortly afterwards in 2014.
We continue to have close links with our sponsors, the Worshipful Company of Skinners, one of the ‘Great Twelve’ livery companies of the City of London, with a history dating back to the 11th century, and formally founded in 1327.
Our Academy’s motto is ‘Be the best you can be’ and the values we uphold and promote are curiosity, kindness, and bravery. We want the young people in our care to develop a love of learning, a consideration for others, and the courage to take on new challenges and stand up for what is right.
We are a rapidly improving school. Following a full Ofsted inspection in April 2026, Skinners’ Academy achieved the ‘Expected’ standard in every area of the inspection framework. Inspectors noted that: ‘The curriculum is broad and ambitious. Leaders foster an inclusive culture across the school. Classrooms, corridors and social times are calm and safe. Pupils feel safe at school.’ Since then, we have continued to build on those successes and provide an outstanding experience for all our students. Our students’ Key Stage 4 outcomes exceed national averages, and our sixth form is one of the top-achieving sixth forms in the Borough for value-added results, with many students progressing to highly regarded universities following their graduation from the Academy.
We offer our students a genuinely enriching and well-rounded educational experience that both supports and challenges them, enabling them to develop into knowledgeable, skilled, resilient, and caring young people, equipped with the qualifications and attributes they need to thrive and succeed in adult life.
We have an ambitious and creative curriculum, designed and delivered with careful consideration of all students’ needs, talents, and interests. We support our students in achieving academic excellence by ensuring they receive outstanding teaching from highly skilled subject specialists. This is complemented by exceptional pastoral support, a comprehensive personal development curriculum, and a wealth of enrichment opportunities for all.
We are proud of the aspirational, inclusive, and caring community we have created at this Academy.
Ms R Adediran
Acting Principal

pageCache.pageTitle: Skinners' Academy Celebrates Best GCSE Results in School History - Latest News - Skinners' Academy Hackney
pageCache.text:
Skinners' Academy Celebrates Best GCSE Results in School History
Skinners' Academy is delighted to celebrate the best GCSE results in the school's history, with students achieving outstanding outcomes across a wide range of subjects and setting new records for academic success.
This year's results represent a remarkable achievement for our Year 11 cohort, with 74% of all grades awarded at Grade 4 or above and an average grade of 5 across all entries. Students also secured a record number of the very highest grades, reflecting both exceptional individual achievement and the strength of teaching and learning across the Academy.
Particularly strong performances were seen in English, Mathematics, the Sciences, History and Business, where students achieved some of the strongest outcomes ever recorded at the school.
These results are the culmination of years of hard work, determination and resilience from our students. Having navigated the challenges and demands of GCSE study, they have demonstrated an unwavering commitment to being the very best they can be.
The success of this year's GCSE cohort builds on the Academy's wider culture of academic excellence and follows a second successive year of exceptional Sixth Form outcomes.
Earlier this summer, Skinners' Academy celebrated another outstanding set of A Level and vocational results, placing the school amongst the top 10% of providers nationally for student progress at Key Stage 5. Sixth Form students also achieved record numbers of A and B grades, enabling many to secure places at leading universities, competitive apprenticeships and other ambitious destinations.
Together, these achievements demonstrate the strength of the educational journey at Skinners' Academy, from Year 7 through to Sixth Form, and reflect the Academy's commitment to ensuring every young person can thrive academically and personally.
As we celebrate this historic milestone, we would like to thank our staff, families and wider community for their ongoing support. Most importantly, we offer our warmest congratulations to our Year 11 students, whose hard work and determination have helped make school history.
Congratulations to the Class of 2026. We are incredibly proud of you and look forward to seeing the success you achieve in the years ahead.
Be the best you can be.

Results & Performance Tables
Definitions
Progress 8
This score shows how much progress pupils at this school made across 8 qualifications between the end of Key Stage 2 and the end of Key Stage 4. A positive progress score indicates students are making more progress than their peers nationally with the same starting point. In the summer of 2025 and 2026, no Progress 8 score will be published because the cohorts of students sitting their Key Stage 4 examinations did not sit SATs at the end of Key Stage 2 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Attainment 8
Schools get a score based on how well pupils have performed in up to 8 qualifications, including English, mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, history, geography, modern foreign languages and other GCSE or Level 2 BTEC qualifications.

pageCache.pageTitle: Outstanding A Level Results at Skinners’ Academy Sixth Form  - Latest News - Skinners' Academy Hackney
pageCache.text:
Outstanding A Level Results at Skinners’ Academy Sixth Form
Skinners’ Academy Sixth Form is celebrating another exceptional year of A Level and vocational results, with students once again among the top 10% nationally for progress.
For the second year in a row, the progress made by our students places Skinners’ Academy Sixth Form in the top 10% of schools and colleges nationally. This is a remarkable achievement and reflects the determination, resilience and hard work of our students, alongside the dedication and expertise of our teachers and support staff.
Our students have worked incredibly hard throughout their time in the Sixth Form, overcoming challenges, supporting one another and striving to achieve their ambitions. Their results are a testament to what can be achieved when students, families and staff work together with a shared commitment to success.
There were outstanding performances across both A Level and vocational courses. A Level Politics achieved exceptional progress for the second consecutive year, while A Level Business and BTEC Sport also achieved outstanding progress. Across the Sixth Form, a large proportion of students met or exceeded their target grades.
Most importantly, these results have opened the door to a wide range of exciting next steps. Our students are progressing to university, apprenticeships, employment and other opportunities, ready to take the next step towards their future ambitions.
We are incredibly proud of every one of our students. Behind every result is a story of hard work, perseverance and ambition, and we are delighted to celebrate their success with them.
We would also like to thank our Sixth Form teachers and support staff for their unwavering commitment to our students. Their high expectations, excellent teaching and pastoral support have played a vital role in helping our students to flourish.
Congratulations to the Class of 2026! We cannot wait to see what you achieve next.
Be the best you can be.

SEND
A Culture of Inclusion
Inclusion is the right to an education for every child. At Skinners' Academy, we achieve this by ensuring:
We believe it is the responsibility of all staff, not just those in pastoral or leadership roles, to ensure that every child and young person is supported to “be the best you can be” each and every day.
We recognise that children and young people bring diverse strengths, identities, and lived experiences to our community, and that some experience barriers within the educational environment that can affect access to learning, participation, and wellbeing. These may be connected to Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities, socio-economic circumstances, contextual safeguarding factors, and/or other aspects of a child’s context, and may be life-long or change over time.
Our role is to listen and learn from our students and families, to remove barriers wherever possible, and to adapt our provision and support so that all children and young people can thrive in school and beyond.
Everyone’s voice is heard.
Everyone’s identity is valued.
Everyone is supported to thrive.
SEND Overview
Skinners’ Academy is an inclusive mainstream secondary school for students aged 11–18, located in Hackney, with a Sixth Form on the same site. We have an above‑average number of students with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) and are committed to ensuring that all students, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), achieve their full potential.
As a mainstream school, students attend mainstream lessons for the majority of the school day, with withdrawal only for targeted interventions or specialist programmes where appropriate. All students are encouraged to participate fully in enrichment opportunities such as after‑school clubs, music sessions and educational visits.
High‑quality, inclusive teaching (“quality‑first teaching”) underpins all classroom practice and is the foundation of support for students with SEND.
What are Special Educational Needs and Disabilities?
Skinners’ Academy supports students across all four broad areas of need identified in the SEND Code of Practice (2015):
We support students with a wide range of needs, including but not limited to:
Communication and interaction
Cognition and learning
Social, emotional and mental health
Sensory and/or physical needs
Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC)
Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH)
Speech, Language and Communication Needs (SLCN)
Specific, Moderate and Severe Learning Difficulties
Hearing Impairment
Visual Impairment
Physical Disability
Multi‑sensory Impairment
Admissions
Admissions to Skinners’ Academy are managed through the Hackney Learning Trust as part of the Pan‑London admissions system. Full details are available in the Admissions Policy on the Academy website.
Admissions for children with an Education, Health and Care Plan are completed through a consultation process led by the Local Authority.
Supporting students with medical needs
The SEND Department works closely with the Academy Nurse and external health professionals to support students with medical needs. Individual Healthcare Plans are created in partnership with families and relevant professionals where required.
Training and expertise of staff
All new staff receive SEND training as part of their induction. Ongoing professional development takes place throughout the year, including whole‑school training and student‑specific guidance where needed.
Accessibility
The Academy site is fully accessible and includes:
We work closely with specialist teachers from Hackney Learning Trust to ensure appropriate adjustments are in place.
Lifts throughout the building
Disabled toilets with hoist facilities
Transition support
We provide structured transition support:
Induction programme for Year 7
Complaints
If concerns cannot be resolved informally, parents/carers can follow the Trust’s Complaints Procedure, available on the Trust website.

Curriculum Overview
“Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.” — Nelson Mandela
At Skinners’ Academy, we believe that every pupil, regardless of their background, deserves to have access to, study and discuss the best that humanity has created. Our curriculum is unashamedly ambitious and academically rigorous, built upon the core idea of powerful knowledge; knowledge that pupils would be unlikely to encounter outside of school, and that is central to their understanding of each subject that they study, but also the world around them. This knowledge gives our pupils power to meaningfully engage with the biggest and most challenging questions facing society and therefore go on to become people who can change the world.
We believe that each subject should be studied on its own terms because each one represents a unique discipline. The curriculum is therefore meticulously crafted by subject experts, giving pupils both the depth and breadth to develop subject expertise. It is our hope that this will inspire pupils to be curious about the subjects they study.
To find out more about any of the subjects listed below, please contact:
Vice Principal, Curriculum - Mr M Rosenthal
Curriculum Maps
Key Stage 3
At Key Stage 3 we have developed a broad and ambitious curriculum for our students focused on developing the most powerful knowledge and skills required to become experts in each of the subjects they study. We also provide extensive support for pupils for reading and literacy, as well as subject-specific support through after school catch up sessions. We believe by maintaining high academic standards and providing bespoke support, pupils will flourish and therefore achieve outstanding outcomes.
All students study the core curriculum in English, mathematics and science.
Pupils will also study: Art - Computing - Design Technology - Drama - Food Technology - Modern Foreign Languages (French or Spanish) - Geography - History - Religious Education - Music - Physical Education - Personal, Social, Health and Citizenship Education (PSHCE)
Key Stage 4
All students study GCSEs in English language, English literature, mathematics, science, and Religious Studies or Citizenship, History or Geography, and have PE as part of their timetable. A broad range of academic and vocational subjects are offered to students in Key Stage 4, with a combination of setting and mixed-ability groupings.
All pupils study either Religious Studies or Citizenship as an early-entry GCSE which they will start in Year 9 and complete in Year 10. This is a valuable opportunity to experience undertaking a GCSE before the rest of their exams in Year 11. Pupils are also encouraged to and supported with undertaking additional GCSEs in any home languages.
Pupils will also have the opportunity to study a combination of: French - Spanish - Art - Business Studies - Economics – Sociology – Psychology - Music - Hospitality and Catering - Design Technology - PE - BTEC Business - BTEC Sport - BTEC Information Technology
Key Stage 4 Curriculum MapsGCSE Course Guide
Key Stage 5
At Key Stage 5, we offer a rigorous and aspirational curriculum that enables students to specialise in subjects aligned to their strengths, interests and future ambitions. Our sixth form provision is designed to deepen subject knowledge, strengthen independent learning skills and prepare students for success in higher education, apprenticeships or employment.

pageCache.text:
Attendance
Why is excellent attendance and punctuality so important?
Excellent attendance and punctuality at the Academy are vital to help pupils achieve the best possible start in life. Pupils who frequently miss school often fall behind with their academic work which impacts on their progress. There is a strong link between good school attendance and achieving good results.
• A child who is absent a day of school per week misses an equivalent of two years of their school life over the course of their education
• 90% of young people with absence rates below 85% fail to achieve five or more good grades of GCSE and around one third achieve no GCSEs at all
Attendance Essentials:
• Pupils must arrive at the Academy by 8.30am for line up at 8.35am and a prompt start to tutor time at 8.40am, in full Academy uniform, with all necessary equipment, and ready to learn. Pupils who are late will be given a detention.
• If a pupil is ill, the parent/carer must telephone the Academy on 020 8800 7411, wait for the prompt and press 1 to leave a message for our Attendance Officer. This call must be made before 8.30am and must be made on every day of absence. Alternatively, parents may email through the Edulink app to the Attendance Team.
• You must ensure that, wherever possible, medical and dental appointments are made after the end of the school day or during the school holidays. Where this isn’t possible, the appointment card must be shown to reception at least 2 days in advance, or the parent/carer must phone to discuss with the Attendance Officer. In the case of medical/dental appointments, the parent/carer should provide their child with a signed note with details of the time they need to leave their lesson and the school site so that the teacher allows the student to leave class. It is the pupil’s responsibility to make sure that they have left class and are ready to leave the building on time for their appointment.
• Pupils must not take holidays in term time. Parents/carers may be fined by the Local Authority if they remove their child from school to go on holiday during term time. More detailed information about attendance is available in the Academy’s Attendance Policy or is available in paper form via our reception.
Help
If you, as a family, are experiencing problems with school attendance, it is of vital importance that you contact and discuss the matter with our Attendance Officer in the first instance. Tutors, Heads of Year and senior staff may become involved depending on the need of your child. Please be assured that everyone in the Academy is here to help, support and advise.
Each year a number of parents contact us regarding family holidays within term time. Government guidelines are very clear in that no leave of absence should be granted unless there are exceptional circumstances.
If you need to withdraw your child from school due to an exceptional circumstance, please complete the form below with a minimum of two weeks' notice.

Edulink & Parent Pay
Skinners’ Academy utilises Edulink One, an app-based software that can be used on a PC, laptop, tablet or mobile device – via a web browser or via the EduLink app.
Edulink One will allow you to contact teachers directly, receive all important updates and allow you to monitor your child's lessons, homework, assessments, reports, book appointments for Parents’ Evening and much more. When you join us, you will be given your dedicated Username and Password. If you forget your log-in details, please contact reception via telephone at 0208 800 7411 or via email. Please do help us in supporting you and enhancing communication between home and the Academy.
Parent User Guide - Edulink One
​Pupils are not allowed to bring any cash into the Academy for reasons of security. We therefore operate a cashless catering system known as ParentPay.
This enables you to upload money onto your child’s account, either by payment online, or by PayPoint in any one of a number of local stores. It can take 2 or 3 days for your payment to register on our systems when paying by PayPoint so please bear this in mind if utilising PayPoint. Pupils will be able to check the balance on their account by swiping their identity cards at the till in the canteen. You will also be able to check the balance by looking at the catering section of your Edulink account, or by logging onto your ParentPay account.
Please Note - Data Handling & Protection
• ParentPay will never contact you by phone, email or mail and ask you to divulge confidential information like passwords or card numbers. If you are ever contacted by someone claiming to be from ParentPay, do not give them any information, report the call to Skinners’, and we will let ParentPay know.
• Certain data will be held on the system to enable accurate operation. This includes name, photo, account balance and meal entitlement. This data will be handled under the guidelines of the Data Protection Act and only used by parties directly involved with the implementation of the system.

pageCache.pageTitle: Skinners' Company History - Skinners' Academy Hackney
pageCache.text:
Skinners' Company History
Skinners' Academy, located in Woodberry Grove, Hackney, stands as a beacon of educational excellence with roots tracing back to the late 19th century.
Originally established in 1890 as The Skinners’ Company’s School for Girls in Stamford Hill, the institution was founded by the Worshipful Company of Skinners to provide quality education for young women in London. Scroll down to the bottom of the page to see some historical photographs of the old school.
Over the decades, the school evolved, becoming London's first voluntary-aided comprehensive school in 1972, reflecting its commitment to inclusivity and academic excellence.
In 2010, embracing the changing educational landscape and the needs of the local community, the school transitioned into Skinners' Academy, a co-educational institution catering to students aged 11 to 19.
The Academy's state-of-the-art facilities, inaugurated by HRH the Duke of Gloucester in 2011, were designed with sustainability and modern pedagogical approaches in mind, including open-plan learning spaces and eco-friendly features like rainwater recycling systems.
Today, Skinners' Academy serves a diverse student body of approximately 1,000 pupils, with more than 60% speaking English as an additional language and over 86% from ethnic minority backgrounds. The Academy continues to uphold its motto, "Be the best you can be," by fostering an environment that encourages academic achievement, personal growth, and community engagement.
The Worshipful Company of Skinners: A Heritage of Service
The Worshipful Company of Skinners’, one of the Great Twelve Livery Companies of the City of London, has a storied history dating back to its Royal Charter in 1327. Originally associated with the fur trade, the Company has long since transitioned to focus on philanthropic endeavours, particularly in education. Beyond founding Skinners' Academy, the Company supports several other educational institutions, including The Skinners’ School in Royal Tunbridge Wells, The Skinners’ Kent Academy and the Marsh Academy, reflecting its enduring commitment to nurturing young minds.
Through centuries of change, the Skinners' Company has remained steadfast in its mission to serve the community, adapting its focus to meet contemporary needs while honouring its rich heritage.
The Skinners’ Academies Trust
Presently, Skinners’ Academy is part of the Skinners’ Academies Trust, a collaborative Trust of five diverse and high-performing schools in Kent and London. Together we educate a total of 4,500 students across primary and secondary phases and both comprehensive and selective schools.
Our new Trust builds on our shared values and history, and preserves the autonomy and traditions of our school, while enabling and promoting deeper practical collaboration to the benefit of all our young people.
